question_text: A government employee is facing an administrative complaint for dishonesty. During the investigation, she was not allowed to present evidence or cross-examine witnesses. She claims her right to due process was violated. Under Article III of the 1987 Constitution, which of the following is correct?

options.text: Due process only applies to criminal cases, not administrative proceedings.
In administrative proceedings, due process requires the opportunity to be heard, present evidence, and confront witnesses.
Due process is satisfied as long as the employee receives a written notice of the complaint.
The government may deny due process in administrative cases for the sake of efficiency.
